principle: Phase B consumes Phase A topology truth and produces visualization-only 3D placement. Projection never feeds clustering, classification, prompt identity, or canonical registry mutation.

state.purpose: Deterministic epoch lineage, provenance, anchor alignment, displacement evidence, and exact Phase A topology binding.

serialization.canonical_json: sorted keys, UTF-8, indent=2, trailing newline
serialization.epoch_id: E- + first 12 uppercase hex chars of SHA256(canonical projection JSON)

frame.initial_axis_sign_rule: For each axis, the canonically earliest maximum-absolute-coordinate prompt must be non-negative.

alignment.anchor_policy: All prompt IDs shared by current and previous projection, sorted by canonical prompt order.

spatial_stability.enforcement: When a previous accepted projection exists and at least minimum_anchors survive, both limits must pass after rigid alignment. Unchanged Phase A topology requires byte-identical projection and state.

epoch_lineage.parent_epoch_id: Previous accepted projection-state epoch when topology changes; null for the first epoch.
epoch_lineage.topology_binding: projection-state.topology_content_hash_sha256 must exactly equal Phase A topology content_hash_sha256

validation.point_parity: Exactly one 3D point per Phase A prompt node; no missing or extra prompt IDs.
validation.phase_a_immutability: Projection generation must not mutate Prompt Kit registry input or Phase A topology bytes.
validation.unchanged_topology_stability: Supplying the prior accepted projection/state for the same topology must return byte-identical artifacts.
validation.changed_topology_stability: Shared anchors are rigidly aligned and displacement limits fail closed.

owned: anchor alignment against previous accepted projection
projection provenance and deterministic rebuild proof
phase_boundary.next_phase: Phase C owns the immersive viewer and may consume Phase B coordinates without redefining topology truth.
